reflector_materials.name: Polished Household Aluminum Foil — Shiny (Bright) Side
reflector_materials.legality_2027: LEGAL (Rule 3.a-h compliant; if placed on/around cup, must use zero adhesives/fasteners on cup and be removed before final measurement per Clarification #5)
reflector_materials.moisture_flammability: Impermeable vapor barrier; non-combustible bulk metal
reflector_materials.shiny_vs_dull_myth_analysis: DEBUNKED WITH NUANCE: Both sides are produced from the same alloy during pack-rolling (shiny side contacts polished steel work rolls; dull side contacts mating aluminum foil layer). Total hemispherical IR reflectance (rho_NIR_total = 0.95-0.97) and mid-IR emissivity (epsilon_MIR = 0.03-0.04 shiny vs 0.035-0.050 dull) differ by < 1.5%, so for a flat radiant insulation shield both sides perform identically. HOWEVER, for an optical concentrating funnel under a 100-125 W heat lamp, the SHINY side exhibits significantly higher SPECULAR (mirror-like) reflectance (~88% specular vs ~62% specular on the dull side), focusing directional rays into the cup rather than diffusely scattering rays back out the top aperture.
reflector_materials.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.1 p. 739 & Table 10.1 p. 546; Engineering ToolBox Emissivity Guide

reflector_materials.name: Household Aluminum Foil — Dull (Matte) Side
reflector_materials.shiny_vs_dull_myth_analysis: Use shiny side facing the lamp beam inside the concentrating cone for maximum specular focus; dull side facing outward into insulation air gaps still provides epsilon_MIR ~ 0.04 radiant barrier suppression.
reflector_materials.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.1 p. 739 & Table 10.1 p. 546

reflector_materials.name: Aluminized Mylar (Vapor-Deposited Aluminum on BoPET Film)
reflector_materials.moisture_flammability: Impermeable; shrinks if heated > 160 C; orient aluminized face toward lamp beam
reflector_materials.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Ch. 10; PET/BoPET optical coating specifications

reflector_materials.name: Polished Aluminum Sheet / Flashing (Alloy 1100 / 3003 / 6061-T6)
reflector_materials.moisture_flammability: Rigid, non-combustible; holds exact conical/parabolic curvature without wrinkling
reflector_materials.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.1 p. 739 (Alloy 6061-T6) & Table 10.1 p. 546 (Aluminum emittance)

reflector_materials.name: Silvered / Aluminized Mirror Acrylic (PMMA Second-Surface vs First-Surface)
reflector_materials.legality_2027: LEGAL (PMMA is #7 Acrylic, NOT #6 Polystyrene; verify polymer stamp)
reflector_materials.rho_NIR_total: 0.80-0.86 (second-surface through 2x PMMA thickness due to C-H NIR absorption bands >1.6 um) / 0.95-0.98 (first-surface metallized)
reflector_materials.moisture_flammability: Combustible above 300 C; Tg ~ 105 C (softens if placed < 10 cm from 125 W bulb)
reflector_materials.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 743 (acrylic PMMA k=0.17 W/mK, rho=1180 kg/m3)

reflector_materials.name: Silvered Soda-Lime Glass Mirror Tiles
reflector_materials.legality_2027: LEGAL (Caution: heavy and breakable; tape edges for safety)
reflector_materials.epsilon_MIR: 0.94 (smooth glass front surface, Lienhard Table 10.1) / 0.01-0.04 (bare silver, Lienhard Table 10.1)
reflector_materials.moisture_flammability: Non-combustible; high thermal mass penalty if coupled to cup
reflector_materials.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 742 & Table 10.1 p. 546

reflector_materials.name: White Cardstock / White Acrylic Paint / PTFE (Teflon) Sheet
reflector_materials.category: Diffuse Reflector (Selective Solar Reflector / High Mid-IR Emitter)
reflector_materials.legality_2027: LEGAL (Poor choice for concentrating funnel due to Lambertian diffuse backscatter)
reflector_materials.moisture_flammability: Paper is hygroscopic & chars >180 C; PTFE is hydrophobic & non-flammable
reflector_materials.engineering_trap: Students often assume white surfaces reflect heat like mirrors. Per Lienhard Table 10.1 (p. 546) & Table 10.5 (p. 598), white paper/paint has epsilon_MIR = 0.90-0.98 (nearly a blackbody in mid-IR!) and scatters visible/near-IR diffusely in all directions (sending ~50% of incident lamp rays back out the top opening).
reflector_materials.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 pp. 742-743, Table 10.1 p. 546, Table 10.5 p. 598

absorber_and_selective_surfaces.name: Matte Black High-Temperature Paint (Carbon Black in Acrylic or Silicone Binder)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.legality_2027: LEGAL (Apply only to device components; never apply paint/coatings to the ES-provided 9 oz cup per Clarification #5)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.alpha_NIR: 0.94 (Carbon black in acrylic binder, Lienhard Table 10.5 p. 598) to 0.96
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.epsilon_MIR: 0.83 (Carbon black in acrylic binder, Table 10.5) to 0.92-0.96 (oil/flat paints, Table 10.1)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.engineering_notes: High near-IR absorptance (0.94), but also high mid-IR emittance (0.83-0.95). Best used on thin copper/aluminum absorber collars shielded from ambient air by an outer transparent glazing or dead-air gap.
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table 10.1 p. 546 & Table 10.5 p. 598

absorber_and_selective_surfaces.name: Carbon Soot / Lampblack Coating
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.legality_2027: LEGAL WITH CAUTION (Must be sealed/isolated so zero soot flakes can fall into or contact the water per Rule 3.e)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.engineering_notes: Reference standard near-blackbody surface (epsilon = 0.95). Fragile and rubs off easily; matte black high-temp paint or selective black oxide is much safer for competition handling.
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table 10.1 p. 546 & Table A.2 p. 741

absorber_and_selective_surfaces.name: Black Anodized Aluminum Sheet / Collar
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.epsilon_MIR: 0.75-0.88 (standard thick porous Al2O3 anodize) / 0.15-0.30 (thin <2 um selective anodic coating)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.engineering_notes: Al2O3 anodic layer over high-conductivity aluminum substrate (k = 167 W/mK) spreads absorbed lamp heat rapidly around the perimeter of the cup.
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.1 p. 739 & Engineering ToolBox Emissivity Guide

absorber_and_selective_surfaces.name: Selective Solar Absorbers (Black Chrome on Ni, CuO on Cu Ebanol C, Nickel Black, Sputtered Cermet)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.category: True Wavelength-Selective Absorber (High NIR Absorptance, Low MIR Emittance)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.legality_2027: LEGAL (Commercial selective solar foil/tape such as Maxorb / Alanod Mirotherm glued to device collar — NOT attached to cup)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.engineering_notes: Selective absorbers absorb 90-96% of short-wave lamp radiation (lambda ~ 0.4-2.5 um) while suppressing long-wave infrared re-radiation loss (lambda ~ 8-15 um at 300-350 K) by a factor of 5x to 10x.
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table 10.5 p. 598 & Table 10.1 p. 546

absorber_and_selective_surfaces.name: Matte Black Construction Paper / Cardstock
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.epsilon_MIR: 0.92-0.94 (Paper, other colors at 40 C, Lienhard Table 10.1 p. 546)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.engineering_trap: Because paper has low thermal conductivity (k = 0.14 W/mK) and creates an air gap against the tapered cup wall, a black paper sleeve placed around the outside of the cup blocks direct radiation from entering the clear plastic sidewall while conducting heat poorly into the water! Direct radiative penetration through the clear cup wall or a thin high-k metallic foil sleeve is superior.
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 742 & Table 10.1 p. 546

absorber_and_selective_surfaces.name: Blackened Thin Copper (25-50 um) or Aluminum (24-50 um) Non-Contact Absorber Collar / Dry Inner Cone
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.category: Ultra-Low-Thermal-Mass High-Conductivity Secondary Radiant/Convective Transfer Element
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.legality_2027: LEGAL per Rule 3.e & Clarification #5 (May surround the outer cup wall closely without adhesive/clips, or extend inside the upper dry air space of the cup ABOVE the 100 mL waterline so long as NO part ever contacts the water!)
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.thermal_mass_for_100cm2_at_35um_J_K: 1.20 J/K (Cu) or 0.86 J/K (Al) — < 0.3% of the 418.4 J/K heat capacity of 100 mL water!
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.engineering_notes: A 35 um blackened copper or aluminum sleeve consumes < 1.2 J/K of thermal mass (heating up in < 3 seconds) while absorbing stray off-axis rays and transferring heat into the cup wall and upper water layer.
absorber_and_selective_surfaces.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.1 p. 739; Official 2027 Rule 3.e & Clarification #5

glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.name: LDPE / PVDC Clear Plastic Cling Wrap (10-15 um Film Resting on Cup Rim or Upper Frame)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.category: Ultra-Thin Transparent Vapor Barrier / Glazing Film
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.legality_2027: EXPLICITLY LEGAL per Official Clarification #5 (10/21/2026) & Official ES Guide: Teams may place wrap on or around the cup during Water Setup Time provided NO adhesives, tapes, rubber bands, or clips attach it to the cup, cup shape/integrity is unaltered, and the wrap is completely removed before final temperature measurement.
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.tau_NIR_0_7_to_2_5_um: 0.90-0.92 ( ~4% Fresnel reflection per surface, minimal bulk absorption at 12.5 um thickness)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.tau_MIR_5_to_15_um: 0.70-0.85 (LDPE is partially transparent in mid-IR except at 3.4, 6.8, 13.8 um C-H bands; PVDC Saran wrap has stronger C-Cl absorption bands at 9-10 um giving tau_MIR ~ 0.45-0.60)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.engineering_notes: Resting a self-weighted or ring-mounted clear film over the cup mouth eliminates ~95-99% of evaporative heat loss (saving 3-6 W, or +3.5 to +7.5 C over 10-15 min!) while transmitting >90% of incident lamp radiation. Keep film slightly below peak focal constriction or use clear PET film if focal spot temperature exceeds 90 C.
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 743 (LDPE); Official Clarification #5 (10/21/2026)

glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.name: Clear BoPET (Mylar / Polyester Transparency) Film (25-100 um)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.legality_2027: LEGAL per Official Clarification #5 (gravity-resting clear cap or upper aperture window; zero adhesive/clips on cup)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.tau_MIR_5_to_15_um: 0.15-0.35 (strong ester C=O and C-O absorption bands block 65-85% of mid-IR re-radiation!)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.engineering_notes: RECOMMENDED GLAZING MATERIAL: Unlike LDPE cling wrap (which softens at 85-95 C), clear BoPET film withstands 150 C continuous service, never sags under a 125 W heat lamp at h=40 cm, lifts off the cup in <1 second with zero clinging during the 1-minute Final Measurement window, and blocks mid-IR re-radiation (true greenhouse trapping).
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.primary_citation: Official Clarification #5 (10/21/2026); Polymer optical & thermal reference data

glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.name: Transparent Polycarbonate Sheet (Lexan, 0.5-1.5 mm)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 743 (polycarbonate PC, Lexan)

glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.name: Borosilicate Glass Sheet (Pyrex, 1.5-3.0 mm)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.category: Classic Selective Solar/NIR Transmitter & Mid-IR Blocker
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.legality_2027: LEGAL (Ensure stable mounting and no breakage risk)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.tau_MIR_5_to_15_um: < 0.02 for lambda > 3.5 um (virtually opaque in thermal mid-IR, epsilon_MIR = 0.94)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.engineering_notes: Textbook greenhouse glazing (Lienhard p. 599: transmits >90% below 2.7 um, virtually opaque in mid-IR). Note: at 2 mm thickness, ~8% is lost to front/back Fresnel reflection (n ~ 1.47 -> R_1 = ((n-1)/(n+1))^2 = 3.6% per surface).
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 742, Table 10.1 p. 546, Section 10.6 p. 599

glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.name: ES-Provided 9 oz Clear Plastic Party Cup Wall (Clear PET #1 or Clear Polypropylene #5)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.legality_2027: ES-PROVIDED MANDATORY CONTAINER (Rule 3.c & 4.g: 9 oz clear plastic party cup, ~3.9-4.0 in [9.9-10.2 cm] tall, ~2.9-3.0 in [7.37-7.62 cm] mouth diameter, holding 100 mL water)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.wall_thickness_mm: 0.25 to 0.40 (typicalcup mass m_cup = 5.5 to 7.5 g -> C_cup = 6.5 to 11.5 J/K)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.tau_NIR_wall: 0.86-0.90 (transmits near-IR directly into water through sidewall as well as top mouth!)
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.critical_engineering_warning: Rule 5.d / Clarification #5 states: 'The structural integrity and shape of the cup may not be altered in the process of placing the cup in the Device.' For a clear PET (#1) cup, the dry upper plastic rim above the 100 mL waterline (water occupies only the bottom ~3.6-4.0 cm of the 10 cm tall cup!) is cooled only by air and has Tg ~ 72-78 C. If an over-aggressive upper reflector concentrates a >80 C hotspot onto the dry upper plastic rim, the PET rim can warp! Design the reflector focal zone at the WATER SURFACE height (z_water ~ z_base + 3.6 cm) or shade the dry top rim with a non-contact reflective aperture ring.
glazing_and_evaporation_suppression_film.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 743; Official 2027 Rule 4.g & Clarification #5

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Corrugated Cardboard (Fluted Board vs Solid Paperboard)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.density_kg_m3: 180 (fluted bulk) / 790 (solid paperboard, Lienhard Table A.2 p. 742)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.k_W_mK: 0.055 (fluted with trapped air) / 0.14 (solid cardboard, Lienhard Table A.2 p. 742)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.charring_ignition_temp_C: Chars/browns at 180-200 C; auto-ignition at 218-246 C (425-475 F)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.moisture_flammability: Combustible if unshielded near lamp; line all lamp-facing cardboard surfaces with aluminum foil (rho_NIR = 0.96) so absorbed heat flux is < 4% and cardboard stays near room temperature (< 40 C).
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 742 & Table 10.1 p. 546

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Corkboard (Medium Density Natural Granulated/Sheet Cork)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.moisture_flammability: Low moisture absorption; high compressive strength for supporting the cup base with minimal contact area
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 742 (Corkboard, medium rho=170 kg/m3, k=0.04 W/mK at 30 C)

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Cotton / Recycled Denim Insulation Batting
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.legality_2027: LEGAL (Natural cellulose fiber; completely distinct from prohibited fiberglass/mineral wool in Rule 3.b.i)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.moisture_flammability: Hygroscopic: 5-8% ambient moisture regain; keep dry and sealed behind foil
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.primary_citation: Standard cellulosic fiber insulation properties; cross-checked with Lienhard Table A.2

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Sheep Wool Batting / Felt
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.legality_2027: LEGAL (Natural keratin protein fiber; label clearly in binder/inspection so ES never confuses with mineral wool)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.charring_ignition_temp_C: Self-extinguishing natural protein fiber; ignition temperature 570-600 C
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.moisture_flammability: Hygroscopic; excellent thermal & fire safety margin
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 744 (Wool, sheep at 20 C: rho=145 kg/m3, k=0.05 W/mK)

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Balsa Wood, Douglas Fir Plywood, Oak, and Dry Sawdust
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.epsilon_MIR: 0.80-0.90 (Wood at 40 C; Oak planed = 0.90, Lienhard Table 10.1 p. 546)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.engineering_notes: Balsa wood (k = 0.05 W/mK, rho = 100 kg/m3) is an exceptional structural insulator for knife-edge 3-point cup support rings and low-mass reflector ribs.
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.primary_citation: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Table A.2 p. 744 & Table 10.1 p. 546

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Closed-Cell Polyethylene (PE, #2/#4) Foam Sheet
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.legality_2027: LEGAL (Polyethylene is #2/#4 polyolefin, NOT #6 Polystyrene! Keep labeled manufacturer spec sheet in binder to prove PE composition at impound/inspection)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.solid_polymer_reference: Solid LDPE (rho=920 kg/m3, cp=2100 J/kgK, k=0.33 W/mK) / HDPE (rho=960 kg/m3, cp=2260 J/kgK, k=0.33 W/mK) per Lienhard Table A.2 p. 743
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.softening_temp_C: 85-105 (CRITICAL: Do not expose bare PE foam directly to focused heat-lamp rays; use only behind aluminum foil or in lower cup cradle)

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Silicone Elastomer Sheet / Closed-Cell Silicone Foam
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.engineering_notes: Thermally stable up to 220 C; ideal for soft centering bumpers or upper thermal seal gaskets around the cup.

compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.name: Trapped Stagnant Air Gap Bounded by Low-Emissivity Aluminum Foil (Multi-Layer Foil-Air-Foil)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.legality_2027: LEGAL (Zero prohibited materials, negligible thermal mass, 100% compliant with Rule 3.b)
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.optimal_gap_thickness_mm: 10 to 13 mm (single gap); multiple 10 mm foil-separated air gaps in series
compliant_insulators_and_structural_mate.rayleigh_benard_convection_limit: For horizontal air layer heated from below, natural convection cells start at critical Rayleigh number Ra_c = g * beta * Delta_T * delta^3 / (nu * alpha) = 1708. At T_f = 305 K (beta = 1/305 K^-1) and Delta_T = 15 K across one gap, Ra_delta = 1708 occurs at delta_c = 11.1 mm. For vertical air slots, conduction dominates (Nu ~ 1) for Ra_delta < 2000 (delta <= 12 mm). With foil walls (epsilon = 0.04), h_rad across the gap is reduced from 6.0 W/m2K to 4*sigma*T_m^3 / (2/epsilon - 1) = 0.125 W/m2K, giving an effective gap conductivity k_eff = k_air + h_rad*delta = 0.0262 + 0.125*(0.010) = 0.0275 W/mK (better than Styrofoam EPS k=0.035 W/mK, with 1/20th the thermal mass and 100% rule compliance!).

water_nir_spectral_absorption_hale_querr.stratification_and_clarification_1_to_4_: Because 66.4% of the 2400 K heat-lamp radiation is absorbed directly within the top 5.0 mm of water (and 72.4% within the top 10.0 mm), top-down heating creates a warm, low-density upper water layer (T_top > T_bottom, rho_top < rho_bottom) resting stably atop cooler bottom water. Because gravity stabilizes this inverted density gradient (Rayleigh number Ra < 0 for top-heated water!), convective mixing is suppressed and downward heat leakage occurs only by slow molecular conduction (alpha_water = 1.45e-7 m2/s -> diffusion length sqrt(4*alpha*t) = 18.7 mm in 600 s). Since Official Clarifications #1-#3 prohibit any stirring, swirling, or shaking and Clarification #4 recommends that the ES measure the TOP LAYER of water near the center of the cup, preserving this top-layer thermal stratification increases the measured T_final by +3.0 to +6.5 C compared to uniform bulk heating (m*c_p = 418.4 J/K)!

evaporative_heat_loss_and_glazing_quanti.physics_basis: Lienhard & Lienhard (2024) Section 11.7 Example 11.11 (pp. 662-664): Sherwood/Nusselt analogy for convective mass transfer of water vapor from an open cup of diameter D = 0.075 m (A_surface = 32-38 cm2 at 100 mL water level).
evaporative_heat_loss_and_glazing_quanti.glazing_cover_suppression_clarification_: Placing a removable, non-attached clear BoPET (25-50 um) or LDPE film cap over the cup mouth during Water Setup Time (Clarification #5, 10/21/2026) traps saturated air above the water surface (RH_headspace -> 100%), cutting Q_evap by >95% (saving ~2000 J over 10 min, worth +4.5 to +8.0 C on the measured top water layer) at the cost of only ~9-10% Fresnel reflection loss.

transient_heating_and_prediction_equatio.lumped_capacitance_governing_ode: C_eff * dT/dt = P_abs(h, P_bulb) - (T - T_room) / R_th
transient_heating_and_prediction_equatio.algebraic_exact_solution: T(t) = T_ss - (T_ss - T_start) * exp(-t / tau) = T_start + (T_ss - T_start) * (1 - exp(-t / tau))
transient_heating_and_prediction_equatio.initial_heating_rate: (dT/dt)_0 = (P_abs - (T_start - T_room)/R_th) / C_eff  [= P_abs / C_eff when T_start = T_room]
transient_heating_and_prediction_equatio.stratified_top_layer_two_Parameter_compe: T_final(t, h, P_bulb, T_start, T_room) = T_start + kappa_strat(t) * (P_abs(h, P_bulb) * R_th + T_room - T_start) * (1 - exp(-t / tau_eff))

sensor_comparison.physical_principle: Volumetric thermal expansion of dyed ethanol/kerosene in glass capillary (Delta_V = V_0 * beta * Delta_T)
sensor_comparison.resolution_C: 0.5 to 1.0 C (0.1 C only on precision laboratory models)
sensor_comparison.time_constant_tau_in_water_s: 6.0 to 12.0 s (5*tau settling time = 30 to 60 s)
sensor_comparison.required_immersion_depth_mm: 76 mm (partial immersion line) or total column immersion; large error if dipped only 5-10 mm into top layer!
sensor_comparison.es_2027_relevance: Permitted under Rule 4.f ('non-mercury, electronic probe, or non-contact'), though slower and harder to read to 0.1 C in the top water layer.

sensor_comparison.physical_principle: Semiconductor band-gap exponential resistance decrease with T: 1/T = A + B*ln(R) + C*(ln(R))^3 (Steinhart-Hart) or R(T) = R_0 * exp(beta*(1/T - 1/T_0))
sensor_comparison.time_constant_tau_in_water_s: 0.8 to 2.5 s (bare bead) / 2.5 to 5.0 s (stainless sheath; 5*tau = 12 to 25 s)
sensor_comparison.required_immersion_depth_mm: 8 to 15 mm (sensor bead sits inside the bottom 3-5 mm of the probe tip!)
sensor_comparison.es_2027_relevance: MOST COMMON ES THERMOMETER: Fast, reads to 0.1 C, and measures the top 5-15 mm water layer accurately per Clarification #4.

sensor_comparison.physical_principle: Positive metallic resistance coefficient of pure platinum: R(t) = R_0*(1 + A*t + B*t^2) for t >= 0 C, with R_0 = 100.00 Ohm at 0 C, A = 3.9083e-3 C^-1, B = -5.775e-7 C^-2 (alpha = 0.00385055 Ohm/(Ohm*C))
sensor_comparison.required_immersion_depth_mm: 25 to 50 mm (platinum wire/film element extends 10-25 mm up the stem + stem conduction error)
sensor_comparison.es_2027_relevance: High metrological stability; deeper stem immersion mixes or averages across a thicker layer than a point thermistor.

sensor_comparison.sensor_type: Type K Thermocouple (Chromel-Alumel, NIST ITS-90 SRD 60)
sensor_comparison.physical_principle: Seebeck thermoelectric effect at welded junction of Chromel (Ni-10%Cr) and Alumel (Ni-2%Mn-2%Al-1%Si): dE/dT = S_AB ~ 39.5 uV/K at 0 C to 41.3 uV/K at 100 C, referenced to cold-junction compensation (CJC)
sensor_comparison.typical_accuracy_C: ±1.1 C (Special Limits of Error) or ±2.2 C (Standard); CJC adds ±0.3-0.5 C offset
sensor_comparison.time_constant_tau_in_water_s: 0.05 to 0.3 s (exposed bead) / 1.5 to 3.5 s (sheathed probe)
sensor_comparison.required_immersion_depth_mm: 3 to 10 mm (exposed tip measures exact surface layer depth)
sensor_comparison.es_2027_relevance: Fastest response time; because Rule 4.f guarantees the SAME thermometer is used for a team's start and final reading, any fixed CJC zero-offset cancels in TG = T_final - T_start but remains in T_final for PE!

sensor_comparison.sensor_type: Non-Contact Infrared (IR) Thermometer (8-14 um Bolometer/Thermopile Pyrometer)
sensor_comparison.physical_principle: Measures band-integrated thermal radiance L_det = epsilon_obj * L_bb(T_obj) + (1 - epsilon_obj) * L_bb(T_amb)
sensor_comparison.required_immersion_depth_mm: 0.0 mm (measures top ~10-20 um skin of liquid water where epsilon_MIR = 0.96!)
sensor_comparison.es_2027_relevance: Explicitly permitted by Rule 4.f ('non-contact'). Because liquid water has epsilon = 0.96 in the 8-14 um band (Lienhard Table 10.1 p. 546), an IR gun preset to epsilon = 0.95 reads the true top surface skin temperature of water accurately (provided the distance-to-spot ratio D:S ~ 12:1 keeps the spot inside the 7.5 cm cup mouth and no plastic wrap remains on the cup!).

jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.application_example: Temperature Gain TG = T_final - T_start: u(TG) = sqrt(u_rand(T_f)^2 + u_rand(T_s)^2) [Note: correlated systematic zero-offset delta_sys cancels in T_f - T_s!]

jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.function: Mean x_bar of n independent measurements
jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.propagation_equation: u_A(x_bar) = s / sqrt(n), where s = sqrt( (1/(n-1)) * sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - x_bar)^2 )

jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.operation: Type B Rectangular (Uniform) Digital Resolution Uncertainty
jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.function: Instrument with least-count resolution Delta_res (e.g. 0.1 C) or half-width limit ±a
jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.propagation_equation: u_B = a / sqrt(3) = Delta_res / (2 * sqrt(3)) = 0.2887 * Delta_res (for 0.1 C display, u_B = 0.0289 C)

jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.operation: Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression Slope & Intercept Uncertainty
jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.function: y = m*x + b fitted to N data pairs (x_i, y_i)
jcgm_gum_uncertainty_propagation_formula.propagation_equation: s_{y|x} = sqrt( sum (y_i - (m*x_i + b))^2 / (N - 2) );  u(m) = s_{y|x} / sqrt( S_xx );  u(b) = s_{y|x} * sqrt( 1/N + x_bar^2 / S_xx ), where S_xx = sum (x_i - x_bar)^2
